summary: Bastion SSH access blocked after Okta group rename; role provisioning fails
description:
Issue summary: Multiple engineers reported immediate 403/permission-denied when attempting SSH via company bastion after a scheduled Okta AD group rename. Impact: ~12 engineers unable to access prod bastion for t=2 hours during incident window. Not customer-facing but blocks oncall and deploys.

Observed behavior: SSH session starts but fails during role resolution with HTTP 403 from identity-proxy. Logs show missing 'groups' claim in SAML assertion for affected users. Okta audit shows group rename event at 2026-03-11T09:02:17Z. SCIM/group-sync job ran at 09:15Z but reported 0 group changes.

Environment: prod-us-east bastion cluster; identity-proxy v2.7.1; sso-idp connector behind idp-proxy-1; group-sync cron job in infra namespace.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Have Okta group A renamed to A-renamed via admin console.
2) Trigger a new SSH session for a user who was a member of original group A.
3) Observe identity-proxy request to RBAC service returns empty role set and bastion returns 403.
4) Inspect SAML assertion forwarded by idp-proxy: 'groups' attribute missing or containing normalized values not recognized by role mapping.
logs:
identity-proxy/error.log lines (2026-03-11T09:17:22Z): 'ERROR role_lookup.go:42 user=abcd123: groups claim not present, fallback_roles=[]'
idp-proxy/access.log (2026-03-11T09:17Z): 'SAML assertion for user abcd123: claims: email=j.doe@redwood.com, groups=[okta:developers_v2]'
okta-audit: '2026-03-11T09:02:17Z group.update id=00g7... name=team-platform -> team-platform-renamed by admin.svc'
comments: 2026-03-11 09:25 - Marcus Chen (assigned): Confirmed reports, reproducing locally with renamed group. Identity-proxy does not map normalized group name to RBAC roles. Escalating to infra-auth. Slack thread: #infra-bastion.

2026-03-11 09:40 - Priya Nair (SRE): Temporary workaround applied: added affected users to fallback 'bastion-access' group and restarted identity-proxy; access restored for 8/12 users. Willting on full sync confirmation.

2026-03-11 10:05 - Infra-auth (comment): Found Okta transformation that prepends 'okta:' and lowercases group keys deployed in last config rollout (config-id cfg-2026-03-10). Role mapping table still uses legacy group keys (camelCase). Need a mapping migration or rollback.

2026-03-12 08:12 - Marcus Chen: Rolled back Okta transformation and kicked group-sync job; group mappings reconciled. Planning a one-hour maintenance to deploy mapping migration and add assertion tests to CI.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Okta group rename + new transformation pipeline changed claim format (prefix/casing), identity-proxy role_lookup doesn't normalize, causing empty role sets.
Confirmed: SAML assertion shape changed; identity-proxy expects 'groups' values matching RBAC store keys. New format included 'okta:' prefix and snake_case conversion.
SCIM group-sync did not pick up rename because transformation occurred before SCIM attribute mapping; sync job ignores transformed displayName and relies on OKTA.group.name attribute.
Temporary mitigation: manual assignment to 'bastion-access' fallback group and service restart restored access while rollback and sync completed.
Risk: If rollout automation re-applies transformation, access will break again for any newly renamed groups. Need CI guard and an automated mapping step.
resolution: Mitigated 2026-03-12 08:00 by rolling back Okta transformation and re-running group-sync. Identity-proxy restarted and RBAC mapping reconciled. Full fix: deploy mapping migration in infra-auth (PR github.com/redwood/infra/pull/5234) which normalizes incoming group claims and updates role_map. Follow-ups: create pre-merge SAML assertion contract test, add a smoke check to group-sync that fails rollout on >0 unmatched groups, and document an Okta group-rename runbook. Incident closed as mitigated; monitoring in place for 48h.
